stem: Point $P({=p_x}, {=p_y})$ and point $Q(x, {=q_y})$ lie ${=dist}$ units apart. Find all possible values of $x$.
solution: Write down the distance formula and substitute the known values: $d_{PQ}=\sqrt{(x-({=p_x}))^{2}+({=q_y}-({=p_y}))^{2}}$, so ${=dist}=\sqrt{(x-({=p_x}))^{2}+({=q_y}-({=p_y}))^{2}}$.
Take the square root of both sides: $x-({=p_x})=\pm\sqrt{{=legx_sq}}=\pm{=leg_x}$.
notes:
Entry-point version of the skill: same isolate-and-square-root method the book uses in ex8-2-3/ex8-2-4/ex8-6-6, but (like ex8-2-7, this family's parent) there is no diagram to narrow the two roots, so both values are the correct complete answer, matching the objective's own 'solving for all valid values'. A solver who states only one root is making the error already catalogued as mc:g10m8s2-1-2:stops-at-first-root — worth flagging in grading even though this is not an mcq family.

PIPELINE NORMALISATION (not an author edit): drop-redundant-answer: removed the top-level "answer" ("x = {=r2} or x = {=r1}"); an expression family's answer is marker.answer ("[{=r2}, {=r1}]"), unchanged.
